title: Most Frequent Prime
summary: Given a m x n matrix, you can generate numbers by moving in one of eight directions (east, south-east, south, south-west, west, north-west, north, and north-east) from each cell.
statement: Given a m x n matrix, you can generate numbers by moving in one of eight directions (east, south-east, south, south-west, west, north-west, north, and north-east) from each cell. Identify the most frequent prime number greater than 10 that can be formed in this manner, or return -1 if no such prime number exists. If there are multiple prime numbers with the same frequency, return the largest one.
constraints: mat is a nonempty matrix up to 6×6 containing digits one through nine.
From every cell, extend in one fixed one of eight directions and count every formed prime greater than ten.
Return the highest-frequency prime, breaking ties toward the larger value, or -1.
hints: Each start and fixed direction generates one decimal prefix per step, and repeated generation contributes repeated frequency.
Enumerate eight rays, extend the numeric value digit by digit, and count values passing trial-division primality.
For every cell and direction, walk in bounds; value=10*value+digit; count primes >10; maximize (frequency,value).
Every legal generated number corresponds to one unique ray prefix, so enumeration preserves exact multiplicity and the tuple maximum implements the tie rule.
editorial: Every legal generated number corresponds to one unique ray prefix, so enumeration preserves exact multiplicity and the tuple maximum implements the tie rule.
